name: FluidAndWater3D
description: Water and stylized fluid toolkit for GDevelop 5 (Three.js WebGL2 backend). Features Gerstner water volumes, Tessendorf spectral oceans, approximate depth absorption and shoreline foam, underwater fog, multi-probe boat buoyancy, and pourable SPH droplets with container fill tracking.
shortDescription: Gerstner and FFT oceans, underwater fog, boat buoyancy, and pourable SPH droplets.
author: Twillion

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: WaterBody3D
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Attach to a 3D Box or Plane to create sizable ocean volumes, lakes, rivers, or swimming pools with Gerstner waves, Beer-Lambert depth absorption, foam, and underwater camera transitions.

propertyDescriptors.name: ArtWaterType
propertyDescriptors.label: Water Type
propertyDescriptors.description: Palette and optics profile: colour, optical depth, caustics, crest and shore foam, and refraction. Choosing a named type OVERRIDES the colour, foam and optics properties below - set this to Custom to author them yourself. It does not touch the wave settings.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveHeight
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Height
propertyDescriptors.description: Master wave amplitude in pixels.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveChoppiness
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Choppiness
propertyDescriptors.description: Gerstner crest sharpness (0.0 = sine, 1.0 = sharp crests).

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveSpeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Speed
propertyDescriptors.description: Time frequency multiplier for wave propagation.

propertyDescriptors.name: WindDirection
propertyDescriptors.label: Wind Direction
propertyDescriptors.description: Wave travel direction in degrees (0 - 360).

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveTiling
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Tiling / Frequency
propertyDescriptors.description: Divides the base wavelength. Higher values tile more, smaller waves across the surface without stretching them.

propertyDescriptors.name: DirectionalSpread
propertyDescriptors.label: Directional Spread
propertyDescriptors.description: How widely the waves fan out from the wind direction, in degrees. 0 puts every wave on the wind for clean rolling swell that all travels one way. 45 is a normal wind sea. 70-90 gives a confused, choppy sea with crests running in many directions. If the surface looks like parallel ridges all marching the same way, raise this.

propertyDescriptors.name: PhaseSeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Phase Seed
propertyDescriptors.description: Shifts every wave octave by a different amount, giving a completely different arrangement of crests from the same settings. Change it if the pattern happens to look wrong where your camera sits. Any number; the same value always rebuilds the same surface.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveIrregularity
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Irregularity
propertyDescriptors.description: Deterministically bends and evolves crest lines so the Gerstner pattern feels less tiled. 0 keeps perfectly straight authored waves; 0.4 is natural; 1 is strongly confused. The CPU height queries and GPU surface use the same calculation.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveScaleMode
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Scale Mode
propertyDescriptors.description: Absolute: wavelength is a fixed 300 units regardless of the volume size, so waves stay world-space and adjacent water bodies tile seamlessly (oceans). RelativeToVolume: one base wave spans the shorter horizontal side of this volume at Wave Tiling 1, so waves stay proportional to the object (pools, ponds, lakes).

propertyDescriptors.name: GridSubdivisions
propertyDescriptors.label: Grid Subdivisions
propertyDescriptors.description: Surface mesh resolution (8 - 256). Sets the shortest wave that can be drawn at all: octaves shorter than 4x the vertex spacing (volume size / this) are filtered out. Raise it on large volumes.

propertyDescriptors.name: MaterialSource
propertyDescriptors.label: Material Source
propertyDescriptors.description: Reserved for future Material3D delegation. The current renderer always uses Builtin colors.

propertyDescriptors.name: ShallowColor
propertyDescriptors.label: Shallow Water Color
propertyDescriptors.description: Color at shallow water depths (Turquoise).

propertyDescriptors.name: DeepColor
propertyDescriptors.label: Deep Ocean Color
propertyDescriptors.description: Color in deep oceanic trenches (Dark Navy).

propertyDescriptors.name: ExtinctionDepth
propertyDescriptors.label: Extinction Depth
propertyDescriptors.description: Depth in pixels at which water fully transitions to deep color.

propertyDescriptors.name: RefractionScale
propertyDescriptors.label: Caustic Distortion Scale
propertyDescriptors.description: Wave-normal distortion applied to caustics; this does not refract the scene color buffer.

propertyDescriptors.name: ShoreFoamIntensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Shore Foam Intensity
propertyDescriptors.description: Foam opacity near the water volume boundary.

propertyDescriptors.name: CrestFoamIntensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Crest Foam Intensity
propertyDescriptors.description: Whitecap foam opacity on steep wave crests.

propertyDescriptors.name: EnableCaustics
propertyDescriptors.label: Enable Caustics
propertyDescriptors.description: Project animated caustic patterns on underwater seabeds.

propertyDescriptors.name: MaskUnderEdges
propertyDescriptors.label: Cut Water Under Edges
propertyDescriptors.description: Cut the water away wherever a WaterEdge3D volume covers it. That volume is an axis-aligned BOX, so a large or irregular piece of land removes a rectangle of water, not its real outline - if the water looks sliced off in a straight line where it meets your coast, turn this OFF. The edge still produces foam and shallows; your actual 3D land hides the water by itself.

propertyDescriptors.name: EnableUnderwaterFX
propertyDescriptors.label: Enable Underwater FX
propertyDescriptors.description: Apply scene fog when the camera is inside and below this water surface.

propertyDescriptors.name: UnderwaterFogColor
propertyDescriptors.label: Underwater Fog Color
propertyDescriptors.description: Volumetric color tint when swimming underwater.

propertyDescriptors.name: UnderwaterFogDensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Underwater Fog Density
propertyDescriptors.description: Visibility falloff density underwater.

propertyDescriptors.name: EnableBodyInteractions
propertyDescriptors.label: Physics Body Ripples
propertyDescriptors.description: Automatically detect moving Physics3D/Jolt bodies intersecting this water volume and create wakes and splash rings. The moving object does not need Buoyancy3D.

propertyDescriptors.name: InteractionStrength

propertyDescriptors.name: InteractionRadius

propertyDescriptors.name: InteractionSpeedThreshold
propertyDescriptors.label: Splash Speed Threshold

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: OceanWaveWorks3D
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Multi-cascade cinematic ocean simulation inspired by NVIDIA WaveWorks. Evaluates dual-cascade spectral FFTs simultaneously (macro deep ocean gravity swells + fine high-frequency choppy wind ripples) to eliminate visible tile repetition and achieve horizon-to-shore realism. Includes international Beaufort wind scale presets (Beaufort 0 to 12), multi-frequency Jacobian whitecap folding, backlit crest subsurface scattering (SSS), and seamless Buoyancy3D and WaterEdge3D compatibility.

propertyDescriptors.name: SwellWeight
propertyDescriptors.label: Cross-Swell Strength
propertyDescriptors.description: How much of the sea is the second, cross-running swell. This is a full sea of its own at the same wavelength as the primary - not ripples on it - which is what lets two comparable crests actually meet and throw water up. Measured hard collisions at Beaufort 9: 0.44% with no cross swell, 1.44% at 0.55, 2.91% at 1.0. Set to 0 to disable it entirely, which also skips its FFTs.

propertyDescriptors.name: SwellAngle
propertyDescriptors.label: Cross-Swell Angle
propertyDescriptors.description: Degrees between the two wave trains. The wave spectrum concentrates energy along the wind and cuts waves running against it to 7%, so with a single direction every crest travels the same way and they can never meet - the sea marches instead of colliding. A real sea crosses because swell from a distant storm runs at an angle to the local wind. Around 48 degrees onward gives the most collisions; below about 30 the two seas are too aligned to meet. This is what drives crest-collision spray. Set to 0 for a single-direction sea.

propertyDescriptors.name: BeaufortScale
propertyDescriptors.label: Beaufort Scale Preset
propertyDescriptors.description: Maritime Beaufort sea scale preset, from Beaufort 0 (mirror calm) to Beaufort 12 (hurricane). Wave height follows the wind speed of the chosen scale rather than being authored directly. Choosing a named preset OVERRIDES the individual colour, foam and sea-state properties below - set this to Custom to author those yourself. For colour, sun and foam styling attach WaterDetailing3D.

propertyDescriptors.name: PersistentFoam
propertyDescriptors.label: Persistent Foam (experimental)
propertyDescriptors.description: Keeps foam in a render target that is blurred with feedback each frame, so whitecaps streak behind the crest and disperse instead of vanishing with it - the way Sea of Thieves does it. How long foam survives comes from the WaterDetailing3D Sub-style: about 3.85s in salt water against 2.54s in fresh. OFF by default: it is the one part of the water that needs a real GPU to verify, and it falls back to the ordinary crest foam if the render target is unusable.

propertyDescriptors.label: Foam Intensity
propertyDescriptors.description: Whitecap froth and shoreline foam brightness.

eventsFunctions.name: LogDiagnostics
eventsFunctions.fullName: Log ocean diagnostics to the console
eventsFunctions.sentence: Log ocean diagnostics for _PARAM0_
eventsFunctions.description: Prints the live sea state to the browser console: tile size, significant wave height, wavelength, mesh scale, and a warning with exact fix numbers if the waves are too big for this water body. The same block is printed once at scene start, but that is BEFORE any "Set Beaufort scale" action runs - call this afterwards to see the sea you are actually showing.

eventsFunctions.name: WaveSteepness
eventsFunctions.description: Significant wave height divided by the tile the spectrum repeats across - the one number that decides whether a sea reads as water. Real wind waves sit near 0.04. Water physically cannot stand up past about 0.10; beyond that the surface folds everywhere, foams everywhere, and displaces outside its own volume, which looks like snow-capped mountains rather than sea.

eventsFunctions.name: SetBeaufortScale
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set Beaufort scale preset on _PARAM0_ to _PARAM2_ over _PARAM3_ seconds
eventsFunctions.description: Sets the sea state from the maritime Beaufort scale. Wave height follows the wind speed of the chosen scale. Adjacent rungs differ by 38-92% in wave height - the scale is roughly cubic - so an instant change is a visible pop: give it a transition time in seconds and the sea grows or calms smoothly through every rung in between. 0 is instant, which is the old behaviour.

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: WaterEdge3D
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Marks an axis-aligned beach, cliff, rock or harbour volume as a water edge. WaterBody3D and OceanFFT3D surfaces mask beneath it, foam along it, and shallows out toward it, so the coastline drives the water rather than the water being a plain rectangle. Attach to a 3D Box covering the land, or to a 3D Model. Up to 8 edges affect a given water body at once, chosen nearest-first — cover a long coast with a few large volumes rather than many small ones.

propertyDescriptors.name: FoamWidth
propertyDescriptors.label: Foam Band Width
propertyDescriptors.description: How far the surf reaches out from this edge, in SCENE UNITS. Leave at 0 to size it against the water body automatically (about 8% of its short side) - useful on a very large bay where a fixed width reads as a hairline, but it widens the surf, so it is opt-in.

propertyDescriptors.name: ShallowWidth
propertyDescriptors.label: Shallow Water Width
propertyDescriptors.description: How far the shallow-water color reaches out from this edge, in SCENE UNITS. Leave at 0 for three times the foam band width. Raising this widens the pale shallow-water tint, not just the foam.

propertyDescriptors.name: Enabled
propertyDescriptors.label: Enabled
propertyDescriptors.description: Whether this edge currently affects the water.

propertyDescriptors.name: HideSourceObject
propertyDescriptors.label: Hide Helper Object
propertyDescriptors.description: Hide the object at runtime when it is only a helper volume. Leave disabled when the object is visible land.

eventsFunctions.name: SetEnabled
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set water edge _PARAM0_ enabled: _PARAM2_
eventsFunctions.description: Turn this edge on or off without destroying the object.

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: WaterDetailing3D
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Visual polish companion behavior for OceanWaveWorks3D and WaterBody3D. Provides Sea of Thieves tier visual fidelity: directional sun azimuth/elevation controls, dual-lobe specular highlights, anti-aliased micro-ripples that eliminate moiré diamond patterns, optical wave depth contrast that prevents washed-out cyan, backlight-aligned subsurface scattering (SSS), and whitecap foam coloring. All parameters are fully editable via actions for in-game settings menus.

propertyDescriptors.name: ArtStyle
propertyDescriptors.label: Style (how it is drawn)
propertyDescriptors.description: The rendering method, and the effect modules that come with it. There is no single "stylized" switch, because each stylized look is its own method: Sea of Thieves draws caustics across the whole surface with a strong backlit crest glow, Realistic fades them out with optical depth so open water goes dark, Swimming Pool removes whitecaps entirely and lets caustics dominate, Toon posterises the surface into flat bands with hard foam edges, and Painterly smears everything soft. A style carries no colours of its own - it shapes whatever Sub-style and Water Type you pick.

propertyDescriptors.name: ArtFoamStyle
propertyDescriptors.label: Foam (what the whitecaps look like)
propertyDescriptors.description: What the foam itself looks like, which none of the other selectors decide. Style is the rendering method, Sub-style is the liquid, Water Type is the condition - a North Sea gale and a reef break can share all three and still have completely different whitecaps. These are not coverage sliders under new names: each one moves cell size, how far the wind draws the foam out, the contrast of the break-up, and how much is left hanging behind the crest. Sea of Thieves is big soft sheets that trail; Whitecaps is sparse and high-contrast with clean water between; Storm Streaks drags everything into long parallel bands; Surf is fine aerated bubbles that linger; Painted is hard-edged flat shapes; Minimal keeps it quiet. Natural is the physically sparse open-ocean foam, and matches versions before 4.1.0.

propertyDescriptors.name: ArtSubStyle
propertyDescriptors.label: Sub-style (what liquid it is)
propertyDescriptors.description: The medium. This is not a colour choice: electrolytes in seawater stop bubbles merging, so salt water whitecaps readily and its foam lingers (~3.85 s) while fresh water rarely whitecaps at all and its foam collapses in ~2.54 s. Pool water is chlorinated and barely foams. The medium also sets base clarity and colour cast.

propertyDescriptors.name: ArtWaterLook
propertyDescriptors.label: Water Type (what it is)
propertyDescriptors.description: The condition the water is in, which owns the colour palette and optics. It layers on the Sub-style: "murky" means something different in a lake than in the open sea. Combined with Style: "Sea of Thieves + Salt Water + Murky" is stylized murky seawater, "Realistic + Fresh Water + Murky" is a silty lake drawn physically. Set any selector to Custom to author the properties below yourself.

propertyDescriptors.name: ArtLighting
propertyDescriptors.label: Lighting (what hour it is)
propertyDescriptors.description: The sun: heading, elevation, colour and the specular lobe it casts. It owns nothing else, so the same water in the same style can be shot at any hour. Set to Custom to drive the sun from the Sun Heading / Elevation / Color properties below, or from a scene DirectionalLight.

propertyDescriptors.name: SunHeading
propertyDescriptors.label: Sun Heading (Azimuth)
propertyDescriptors.description: Sun horizontal direction in degrees (0 = East, 90 = North, 180 = West, 270 = South). Low sun angles directly opposite the camera create dramatic specular trails.

propertyDescriptors.name: SunElevation
propertyDescriptors.label: Sun Elevation (Altitude)
propertyDescriptors.description: Sun altitude angle above horizon in degrees (0 = horizon sunrise/sunset, 90 = zenith noon). Low elevations (15-25°) produce the Sea of Thieves golden-hour trail.

propertyDescriptors.name: SunColor
propertyDescriptors.label: Sun Light Color
propertyDescriptors.description: Sun and specular glint tint color (warm amber/gold for sunset, bright pale yellow/white for midday).

propertyDescriptors.name: SunSpecularIntensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Sun Specular Intensity
propertyDescriptors.description: Brightness of the solar disk reflection and wide ocean glint trail.

propertyDescriptors.name: SunSpecularRoughness
propertyDescriptors.label: Sun Specular Sharpness
propertyDescriptors.description: Shininess / specular exponent (32 = broad soft sheen, 160 = crisp sun glint trail, 512 = intense mirror reflection).

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveContrast
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave Depth Contrast
propertyDescriptors.description: Modulates optical water depth between wave crests and wave troughs. Eliminates washed-out flat cyan by deepening troughs into oceanic navy while keeping crests luminous.

propertyDescriptors.name: DeepColor

propertyDescriptors.description: Color of deep ocean water and shaded wave troughs.

propertyDescriptors.name: ExtinctionDepth
propertyDescriptors.label: Extinction Depth
propertyDescriptors.description: Beer-Lambert optical depth in pixels where water shifts from translucent turquoise to deep oceanic navy.

propertyDescriptors.name: TranslucencyColor
propertyDescriptors.label: Translucency / SSS Color
propertyDescriptors.description: Subsurface scattering inner glow color when looking toward the sun through wave crests.

propertyDescriptors.name: TranslucencyIntensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Translucency Intensity
propertyDescriptors.description: Brightness multiplier for wave crest translucency and backlight scattering.

propertyDescriptors.name: TranslucencyPower
propertyDescriptors.label: Translucency Falloff Power
propertyDescriptors.description: Sharpness of the directional backlight alignment cone for SSS (higher = narrower forward scatter).

propertyDescriptors.name: MicroDetail
propertyDescriptors.label: Micro-Wave Ripples Detail
propertyDescriptors.description: Strength of anti-aliased capillary micro-ripples and surface perturbation.

propertyDescriptors.name: MicroFrequency
propertyDescriptors.label: Micro-Wave Ripples Frequency
propertyDescriptors.description: Spatial frequency scale for capillary micro-ripples (0.5 = broad gentle swells, 1.0 = crisp clear ripples, 2.0+ = fine surface disturbance).

propertyDescriptors.name: Opacity
propertyDescriptors.label: Water Surface Opacity
propertyDescriptors.description: Overall water transparency (0.0 = clear glass, 1.0 = opaque oceanic surface).

propertyDescriptors.name: TextureAnisotropy
propertyDescriptors.label: Anisotropic Filtering (Water Detail)
propertyDescriptors.description: Requested anisotropic filtering level for ocean detail and persistent foam at grazing angles. Uses mipmaps, clamps to device and texture-format support, and preserves foam history when changed.

propertyDescriptors.name: FoamColor
propertyDescriptors.label: Foam Color
propertyDescriptors.description: Tint color of wave whitecaps and crest foam (bright seafoam white).

propertyDescriptors.name: FoamIntensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Foam Brightness / Opacity
propertyDescriptors.description: Brightness multiplier for wave crest whitecaps and edge foam.

propertyDescriptors.name: FoamCoverage
propertyDescriptors.label: Foam Coverage Threshold
propertyDescriptors.description: Surface threshold for whitecap foam coverage (0.0 = rare foam on highest peaks, 1.0 = heavy foam across all crests).

propertyDescriptors.name: SprayEnabled
propertyDescriptors.label: Enable Wave-Collision Spray
propertyDescriptors.description: Spawn upward droplet spray when ocean wave crests collide (converging eigenvalues in the displacement gradient tensor).

propertyDescriptors.name: SprayAmount
propertyDescriptors.label: Spray Spawn Rate
propertyDescriptors.description: Emission rate multiplier for wave-collision spray droplets (0.0 = none, 1.0 = heavy plumes).

propertyDescriptors.name: SprayHeight
propertyDescriptors.label: Spray Launch Height
propertyDescriptors.description: Velocity and height multiplier for upward wave spray droplets.

propertyDescriptors.name: SprayThreshold
propertyDescriptors.label: Spray Trigger Threshold
propertyDescriptors.description: Sensitivity threshold for wave collisions (lower = easier to trigger spray, higher = only violent head-on collisions spurt).
